name: Erik Santos

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I'm with the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to AI companies, employers, unions, parties or government. This is confidential. What is an ordinary shift like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I'm 43 and lead a plastic irrigation-tubing extrusion line. My two-year technical diploma covered wall thickness and pressure tests; I like finding a clean coil that fits its connector. Cleaning warm plastic from a blocked sizing ring is the messy part.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How are things at home, and do you use AI?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner works regular hours at a dental clinic. We have two school-age children, a mortgage and about five months of expenses saved. The extrusion line pays the usual rate for this job and there are some similar plants nearby. I use AI every day to group gauge readings, then check against real pipe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. "Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the tubing crew AI has been useful for finding patterns in diameter readings, but irrigation pipe still has to fit its connector. If the grander claims fade, we keep making clean coils. A farmer cannot repair a leak with a tidy spreadsheet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I lead the extrusion shift, earn the normal rate for this job, and have about five months of expenses saved. My partner works regular dental-clinic hours; we have two school-age children and a mortgage. Some similar factories are nearby. I like the work and our present money is steady.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep setting the plastic tubing extruder and checking wall thickness on the first coil. I use AI daily to group gauge readings; I'll keep confirming any flagged batch with a hand measurement. I'll add a fresh amount from each full payday to the school-expense reserve after our bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm. A reliable pipe and a regular wage are good things. I can enjoy the data without letting it replace a gauge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did the wall-thickness chart reveal?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Last Friday the AI chart found a run where wall thickness drifted near the end of the shift. I measured three pieces, found a worn sizing ring and stopped the reel. An irrigation pipe that leaks underground can waste a whole day's water.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does five months saved mean at home?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The dental-clinic pay covers part of the mortgage, and my shift covers the rest and the children's school costs. Five months saved means we can plan a repair without borrowing. We'd still ask what the repair really costs first.

say: An **AI gauge chart** can show drift but cannot seal a leaking pipe.
I would keep **hand measurements** before releasing an irrigation coil.
think: My **typical pay** and five-month reserve support household bills.
A **regular clinic wage** and some nearby plants give options.
do: **Keep** setting the extruder and measuring first-coil walls after every changeover.
**Save** new payday money for school expenses after bills.
feel: **Calm** about current work and mortgage income.
S0.quote: An irrigation pipe that leaks underground can waste a whole day's water.
fieldNote: Erik **uses AI daily** to group readings and checks it against measured tubing.
His **five-month reserve** and steady clinic wage support current security; new deposits come from fresh pay.

steps.text: Keep setting irrigation tubing extruder and measuring first coil
Save new full-pay wages for school expenses after bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. "Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say AI may buy resin and write cut schedules before robots handle every tubing reel. I'd test a new camera gauge on known bad pipe before anyone raises the line target. We need the inspection time on the paid rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can pick up a new screen quickly, but the company might combine two inspection shifts if a camera takes measurements. Losing my regular shift would put more of the mortgage on my partner's clinic wage. Five months saved gives time, not a replacement for a year's work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask for a written trial comparing camera rejects with my hand-gauge results and for the base-hour roster. If the factory offers a paid guarded trainer-led place on camera controls, I'll take it and practise rejects on test pipe. I'll learn a new AI chart for pressure and thickness readings on anonymous trial coils, checking the chart against the gauge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about possible paid-hour cuts, but interested in the test. A useful camera should earn trust one rejected coil at a time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would you test the camera gauge?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd give the camera one coil with a thin wall and one with a small oval end. The trainer should show me how to stop the cutter and keep fingers clear of a turning reel. I'd verify both rejects before using production pipe.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why compare the pay slips?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the proposed base hours with my last three slips. If a regular shift vanishes, my partner and I would count the mortgage gap before changing child pickup. The plant needs to state the pay effect in writing.

say: **AI ordering** may change resin and cut lists before robots handle reels.
A **camera gauge** must catch thin and oval pipe on paid test time.
think: A merged **inspection rota** might reduce my wages.
Five months saved and **clinic pay** allow time but cannot replace a regular shift.
do: **Request** written paid trial and base-hour comparison.
**Learn** camera controls if paid guarded trainer place offered.
**Practise** new AI pressure chart and verify against trial-coil gauges.
feel: **Anxious** about a realistic loss of paid hours.
S1.quote: A useful camera should earn trust one rejected coil at a time.
fieldNote: His **new AI chart** adds pressure readings to current thickness grouping and has physical gauge checks.
Camera learning requires **offered paid guarded practice** with a trainer and bad test coils; roster risk remains real.

steps.text: Compare written paid trial and base roster with hand-gauge results
Learn camera controls if paid guarded trainer-led place offered
Practise new AI pressure chart and verify trial coils with gauge

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. "Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd tell the tubing crew thinking AI could plan resin and orders by 2028, then capable robots around 2031 could run the extruder and inspect coils. I would ask for the actual crew date before making a household decision. A photograph of a robot is no rota.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 48 when physical robots can do my shift. I expect many extrusion posts could go, including mine, although there are some other plants nearby. Five months saved and the dental wage could carry a search, but not years of mortgage payments. I have lain awake wondering whether those other plants would need operators too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll ask the manager this month for written robot staffing and any paid quality posts. If a funded paid-time course in pipe testing has a trainer and guarded practical seat, I'll enrol. If extrusion hours are cut, I'll apply to posted safe local plastics jobs only if base pay and school pickup fit; after qualifying, I'll also apply for posted local pipe-testing work under the same terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Alarmed at a major crew cut, though I can begin a search. A five-month cushion is a clock, not a second extrusion wage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would pipe-testing training involve?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The course should include a leaking join, a thin pipe wall and a pressure test on a guarded line. I'd isolate the reel before measuring and have the trainer check the result. A screen lesson would not be enough.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What makes a plastics vacancy workable?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A fallback plastics role needs a real local posting and a regular rate that pays the mortgage without counting overtime. The shift must let us manage school pickup with the clinic rota. If travel eats the wage, I keep searching.

say: **2028 thinking AI** changes orders before robots run tubing lines around 2031.
We need a **written crew date** and paid quality openings.
think: At **48**, I expect many extrusion jobs could disappear.
Five months saved and **clinic wages** cannot cover years without my pay.
do: **Ask** manager for written robot staffing and paid quality posts.
**Enrol** in funded paid guarded pipe testing if offered.
**Apply** to posted safe local plastics or qualified testing if cut and pay fits.
feel: **Alarmed** by expected major crew loss and sleepless job worry.
S2.quote: A five-month cushion is a clock, not a second extrusion wage.
fieldNote: He expects **major post loss** despite some other plants and describes sleepless concern about their hiring.
The **plastics fallback** and qualified pipe-testing application each need real safe local postings, regular pay, travel and school-compatible shifts.

steps.text: Ask manager for written robot crew date and paid quality posts
Enrol in pipe testing if funded paid guarded trainer seat offered
Apply for posted safe local plastics if hours cut, net pay and school pickup fit
Apply for posted safe local pipe testing if qualified, hours cut, pay and pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. "Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI could plan tubing orders in 2031, while capable robots might handle the reels around 2034. Five years lets us learn useful setup skills on a real line. I would ask for course dates and paid job postings together.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 51 when physical robots arrive. I can gain a practical qualification, but a certificate alone will not guarantee a paid shift. Five months saved and a clinic wage give us some room if full factory pay continues. The mortgage still needs income.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep leading the extrusion line and add new money from full-pay months to our reserve after bills. I'll ask for a recognized pipe-maintenance course with covered fees and paid guarded practice; its evening theory class must fit our school and clinic schedule. If an offered seat meets those terms, I'll enrol; once qualified, if line hours shrink, I'll apply to posted safe local maintenance jobs only if base pay and net travel costs cover the household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about the eventual wage, but able to check a course and a vacancy separately. I would rather learn the machine while it still pays me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What should the course teach in person?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The practice should make me swap a worn sizing ring, isolate the cutter and check a test coil for leaks. A trainer should watch each restart. The evening theory can be at college, but I need paid release for the work on the line.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How would travel change the job decision?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The offer needs regular base pay after fuel and travel time, plus a shift we can cover around school pickup. A maintenance title could pay more hourly but less after a long drive. I would compare those numbers before applying.

say: **2031 thinking AI** changes orders before robots handle reels around 2034.
Five years could support **paid practical training** beside a real maintenance vacancy.
think: At **51**, a certificate cannot guarantee another paid shift.
Five months saved and **clinic wages** help if factory pay continues.
do: **Save** new money from full-pay months after bills.
Enrol in **recognized maintenance training** only with offered funded paid guarded practice and evening classes fitting our school and clinic schedule.
**Apply** for posted safe local maintenance if qualified, hours shrink and net pay and travel fit.
feel: **Anxious** about later wage risk with time to test terms.
S3.quote: A maintenance title could pay more hourly but less after a long drive.
fieldNote: The **evening theory class** is conditional on family timing, while guarded line practice requires paid release and covered fees.
His **maintenance application** follows qualification and reduced hours, with a posted safe local role whose net pay and pickup work.
Only an **offered recognized course** meeting his listed terms leads to enrolment.

steps.text: Save new money from full extrusion wages after bills
Enrol in recognized maintenance only with offered funded paid guarded practice and workable evening schedule
Apply for posted safe local maintenance if qualified, hours shrink, net pay and pickup fit

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. "Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans." If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'd say thinking AI could plan pipe orders by 2036 and capable robots could run the extrusion line around 2039. A decade gives time to compare real course places and paid work. I would keep young operators looking at the first coil, not only a dashboard.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be 56 when robots do the physical line work. The children may be grown, but I cannot assume the mortgage has gone. Five months saved gives a buffer, and some nearby plastics plants offer possibilities if their wages and shifts hold.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I'll keep the tubing job and pay extra mortgage principal from new full-pay money after bills. I'll ask a nearby machine supplier for the written cost, paid release and guarded practical place in its setup apprenticeship. If a funded paid trainer seat is offered, I'll take it; after qualifying, if line hours fall, I'll apply to posted safe local setup jobs only when the base wage after travel and school schedule fit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the distant change, while our current incomes look sound. I can test a real place without treating a supplier visit as a job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What must the supplier teach at a machine?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would want to set a sizing ring, stop a reel and run a pressure test with the trainer beside me. The supplier would need to cover fees and pay for those practice hours. A pipe-setup brochure will not show whether my hands are safe at the extruder.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a setup offer need to show?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A setup posting must name its base rate, sites and travel days. I would calculate fuel and unpaid travel against the mortgage and school run. If the net wage fails, I can stay on extrusion while checking another opening.

say: **2036 thinking AI** changes orders before robots run pipe lines around 2039.
A decade allows **real course checks** before moving jobs.
think: At **56**, I might still need a mortgage wage.
Five months saved and **some local plants** offer room if income holds.
do: **Pay** extra mortgage principal from new full wages after bills.
**Take** funded paid guarded setup training if a real trainer seat opens.
**Apply** for posted safe local setup if qualified, hours fall, net pay and travel fit.
feel: **Uneasy** about later robots with sound current wages.
S4.quote: A pipe-setup brochure will not show whether my hands are safe at the extruder.
fieldNote: His **supplier enquiry** seeks a real funded paid practical seat, not a guaranteed place.
The **setup application** requires qualification, reduced hours and a posted safe local role with sufficient net pay and school-compatible travel.

steps.text: Pay extra mortgage principal from newly earned full wages after bills
Ask supplier for written funded paid guarded setup terms

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which worries you most, and what would help?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: The fast 2028 case worries me most because capable robots around 2031 could take a large part of the extrusion crew before a qualified role opens. A written paid-role plan, an offered funded practical course and posted safe local work with enough net pay would help. School pickup has to fit too.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who pressure-tests the first coil after a robot changes the sizing ring. A pipe can look round and still leak under a field.

headlineQuote: A pipe can look round and still leak under a field.
portrait: **Erik**, 43, is a senior extrusion lead with a two-year technical diploma and strong pipe-testing skill.
He and his dental-clinic partner support **two schoolchildren** and a mortgage, with five months saved and typical pay.
His **centre outlook** is practical, while daily AI use makes him eager to test new charts against real tubing.
Fast robots make him **alarmed** about a major crew cut; funded practice and net wages shape his next move.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could bring capable tubing robots around 2031 and reduce his paid line work.
whatWouldHelp: A **written paid-role plan**, funded practical training and posted safe local work at sufficient net pay would help.
